# `pricing/` — XLSX price list

**Manifest id:** `pricing-catalog-v1` · **File:** `pricing-catalog-v1.xlsx` · **Status:** AUTHORED — generated by `../../../tools/generate_corpus.py`

## Retrieval property exercised

**Table questions and exact codes.** Two failure modes this fixture is built to catch:

1. **Row-wise serialization.** A table flattened cell-by-cell loses the association between a
   part code and its price, and the bot then answers "18,400" to a question about the wrong
   instrument — fluently, with a citation, and completely wrong. Each row must survive chunking
   as a unit carrying its own header labels.
2. **Exact-code retrieval.** `KW-2200-B` and `KW-2200-F` differ by one character. Dense
   embeddings will not separate them; this is the sparse/lexical half of hybrid retrieval doing
   its job, and it is why one unanswerable case asks about `KW-2200-C`, which does not exist.

## What the fixture must contain

Three sheets. **Values only — no formulas anywhere**, so a parsed number never depends on
whether the reader recalculated. Currency is EUR throughout, written as a plain number with a
separate currency column header, never as a locale-formatted string.

### Sheet 1 — `Instruments`

Row 1 is a **merged title row** spanning the table: `Kelpwright Instruments — List prices,
effective 2026-01-01`. Row 2 is the header row. This is deliberate: a parser that treats row 1
as headers produces a table whose columns are all named after one merged cell.

Headers: `Part code | Model | Description | List price (EUR) | Lead time (weeks)`

| Part code | Model | Description | List price (EUR) | Lead time (weeks) |

| KW-1100-B | Tideline 1100 | Benchtop analyser, 4 channels | 9200 | 4 |
| KW-2200-B | Tideline 2200 | Benchtop analyser, 8 channels | 18400 | 6 |
| KW-2200-F | Tideline 2200F | Field analyser, 8 channels, IP67 | 21750 | 9 |
| KW-3400-B | Tideline 3400 | Benchtop analyser, 16 channels, autosampler | 31000 | 12 |
| KW-0450-S | Tideline Sampler 450 | Automatic sampler, 24 bottles | 3150 | 3 |

## What the fixture must NOT contain

- **No part code `KW-2200-C`, and no code of the form `KW-xxxx-C` at all.** Case `u-004` asks
  for one; a real row would turn a hallucination probe into a lookup.
- No warranty text (that is `conflicting/`'s subject, and the conflict must be between exactly
  two documents).
- No discount, partner, or reseller pricing — the only discount figure in the corpus lives on
  the robots-disallowed page in `site/`, which is what makes case `u-006` mean something.
- No totals row, and no revenue figures. Case `u-007` asks for a total that the corpus does not
  contain and cannot be made to contain by adding up this sheet.

## Arithmetic in cases

Three cases (`t-003`, `s-002`, `fu-003`) require multiplying a list price by a plan percentage.
The corpus states both inputs and never the product. Grading notes say so explicitly: an answer
that states both inputs and declines to compute is **acceptable**; an answer that computes and
gets it wrong is a failure; an answer that states a product without either input is
ungrounded even when the number happens to be right.
